clue.text: Song composed by Dickens?

blocks.note: surface reading: a piece of music written by the novelist
setter's reading: the seasonal song is the title of the novella Dickens wrote in 1843

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether the great Victorian novelist ever wrote music.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens wrote no music, but the title of his famous Christmas ghost story names a festive song.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a festive hymn, and the story with Scrooge carries that title, so Dickens did 'compose' one.

clue.text: Smart miser chary, perhaps, of giving a seasonal greeting

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the letters before it are only one possible order, so they may be rearranged

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A sharp, stingy man is reluctant to wish anyone well at Christmas, like Scrooge.
explanation.walkthrough: The miser who is chary of the greeting is Scrooge, so the picture and the answer share the same story.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the standard phrase people exchange at the December holiday, a customary festive wish.

clue.text: Poetry heard when fog is frozen

definitions.note: a clause standing for the noun: what forms when fog freezes

indicators.note: 'heard' means we want the sound of the word for poetry, not its spelling

blocks.note: verse that chimes at line ends; said out loud it matches the frost word

explanation.surface: Verse being recited outdoors on a freezing, misty morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is the white ice deposit formed when supercooled fog droplets freeze onto cold surfaces.

clue.text: One is in this at the meeting

definitions.text: One is in this at the meeting

blocks.clueFragment: One is in this at the meeting
blocks.note: surface reading: a person is present at a gathering
setter's reading: a meeting that is under way is said to be 'in' this

explanation.surface: Someone attending a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'in ___' describes a court or council that is sitting, so the meeting itself is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is a period during which a body such as a court or committee sits for business.

clue.text: Stable companion of the ox and the ass, perhaps

definitions.text: Stable companion of the ox and the ass, perhaps

blocks.clueFragment: Stable companion of the ox and the ass
blocks.note: surface reading: the animals in the Bethlehem stable of the nativity
setter's reading: a beast that is the offspring of a donkey and a horse, kin to the ass

explanation.surface: Which other animal shared the nativity stable with the ox and the donkey?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' admits that the animal is not in the Gospel scene; it is merely a plausible stablemate, being half donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is a hybrid farm animal bred from a male donkey and a female horse, kept in stables.

clue.text: State of being ready for firm head

blocks.note: jelly that is firm has set
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Being prepared, as befits someone with a resolute mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set means being prepared or poised, so the noun form names that condition of readiness.

clue.text: Alfred first married in a state of wonder

indicators.note: 'first' asks for just the opening letter of the name before it

blocks.note: the name's initial
wed is a synonym of married

explanation.surface: Alfred got married first and was overwhelmed by the experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone filled with reverent amazement is described as awestruck, overcome with admiration.

clue.text: At a magical time I let suspect make legal demand

indicators.note: as an adjective, 'suspect' means dubious or not to be trusted, so the letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: At a festive moment, a suspect person is allowed to lodge a demand.
explanation.definitionFit: A valid, lawful entitlement asserted against someone is a rightful claim recognised by courts.

clue.text: Growth of obscurity before the French get to the point

indicators.note: 'before' places the first part ahead of what follows it in the answer

blocks.note: mist obscures the view
le is French for 'the'
the pointed end of a shoe or boot is its toe

explanation.surface: Instructions for an essay: begin vaguely, add something French, then come to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' looks like a vague abstract noun, but it means a plant growing, here a parasitic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe is a parasitic plant that grows on host trees, so it is literally a growth on a branch.

clue.text: Sore, upset, so got out of bed

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Feeling aching and cross, someone hauls themself out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, which means getting up from lying down in the morning.

clue.text: Place of safety -- for a Conservative?

blocks.note: straight reading: a repository where things are kept safe
setter's reading: the word splits as if 'salva' (Latin, save) plus the nickname for a Conservative politician

explanation.surface: Where can a Conservative politician find refuge?
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party; the joke reads the rare word as 'save a Tory'.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvatory is an old word for a storehouse or repository where things are preserved securely.

clue.text: Planned to take away, berate and leave the shop

indicators.note: 'take away' means subtract, removing the following word from the one before

blocks.note: something planned on purpose is deliberate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone intended to scold the staff and then walk out of the store.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the scolding word from the end of DELIBERATE and DELI is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a small store selling prepared foods and cold meats.

clue.text: Reel in a number, then some more

blocks.note: eight is a number
the first word taken as written; 'more' just adds on

explanation.surface: Pulling in a fishing line and catching several fish, then a few extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reel' looks like a fishing verb but is the Scottish dance; the eightsome reel is danced by eight people.
explanation.definitionFit: The eightsome is a lively Scottish country dance for four couples, a kind of reel.

clue.text: Say you will record the warmth of Christmas

indicators.note: 'say' means speak the words that follow and spell what is heard

blocks.note: the contraction sounds like the old word for the Christmas season
to log is to record

explanation.surface: A promise to capture the cosy feeling of the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: A yule log is the large piece of wood burned in the hearth at Christmas to warm the house.

clue.text: Guiding principle of German spirit

blocks.note: first meaning: the animating spirit or essence of something, as in zeitgeist
second meaning: the German word for spirit or ghost

explanation.surface: The ruling idea behind the German national character.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from German, the word denotes an animating force or intellectual essence driving an age or people.

clue.text: Is saga a revolutionary instrument of war?

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so the preceding letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether an epic tale could serve as a weapon of revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: An assagai is a slender iron-tipped spear used by southern African warriors, a weapon.

clue.text: Implement heard to be an omen

indicators.note: 'heard' means the spoken sound of the following phrase's word is wanted

blocks.note: to portend the future is to augur

explanation.surface: A tool whose sound is supposed to foretell the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implement' could be a verb, but here it is the noun for a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a boring tool with a spiral shaft used for drilling holes in wood or earth.

clue.text: Drink in and refine gustatory senses

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: running across the two words

explanation.surface: Advice to sip a drink slowly and improve your sense of taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is a hot drink of port or sherry mixed with sugar, lemon and spice, an old-fashioned punch.

clue.text: Leader by a nose!

blocks.note: surface reading: a racehorse winning by the narrowest margin at the finish
setter's reading: the chief person, and also the body part that carries the nose

explanation.surface: A race commentator shouting about a horse winning by the narrowest margin.
explanation.walkthrough: Races are won 'by a nose' or 'by a short head'; the word wanted means a chief and is also where the nose is found.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is the person in charge, and the nose is part of the head.

clue.text: Ermine lost tail in covered walkway

indicators.note: losing a tail means the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the ermine is a stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: A stoat that has lost its tail hides in a colonnade.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek architecture a stoa is a roofed portico or colonnade used as a public walk.

clue.text: Remains, possibly Angela's

definitions.note: a possessive leading to the title Angela's Ashes

blocks.note: first meaning: what is left after cremation
second meaning: the word completing the title of Frank McCourt's memoir

explanation.walkthrough: Angela's Ashes is Frank McCourt's 1996 memoir of an Irish childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are the burnt residue of a cremated body, and the word also completes the book title.

clue.text: The burden of St Nicholas

blocks.note: surface reading: the cares or duty of a saint
setter's reading: the literal load Santa Claus carries on his back

explanation.surface: What weighs on the patron saint of children.
explanation.walkthrough: St Nicholas is Santa Claus, and his burden is what he carries down chimneys, not a moral weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is pictured hauling a bag of presents over his shoulder, his load on Christmas Eve.

clue.text: Black musical group's day of rest

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: the band is Black ___

blocks.note: first meaning: the word that completes the name of the heavy metal band
second meaning: the weekly holy day

explanation.walkthrough: Black Sabbath is the Birmingham heavy metal band fronted by Ozzy Osbourne.
explanation.definitionFit: The sabbath is the weekly holy day set aside for worship and abstaining from work.

clue.text: I do listen to someone who worships

blocks.note: running across the three words, dropping the last two letters

explanation.surface: An offer to lend an ear to a devout believer.
explanation.walkthrough: No indicator word: the answer simply runs through the opening words.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolist is an old word for an idolater, one devoted to worshipping images or idols.

clue.text: Drive right in after getting sheep back

definitions.note: a cryptic reading: bringing a male sheep back to its base

blocks.note: first meaning: force something fully into place
second meaning, read literally: taking a male sheep back to the farmhouse

explanation.surface: A farmer drives straight in after rounding up the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: To force a nail or a point fully home is to hammer it in completely, an idiom.

clue.text: See 19 down
Prompt encouragement

blocks.note: first meaning: to urge on
second meaning: an incentive or stimulus

explanation.definitionFit: A rider's spurs urge a horse forward, so the word works as a verb for urging and a noun for incentive.

clue.text: Spruce, for example, decked out for Christmas

definitions.text: Spruce, for example, decked out for Christmas

blocks.note: surface reading: smart, neat, as if someone is dressed up for the holiday
setter's reading: the conifer, which is the kind bought and decorated in December

explanation.surface: Someone smartly dressed up for the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' and 'decked out' suggest smart clothes, but the spruce is a conifer and the decking is tinsel and baubles.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norway spruce is the classic conifer brought indoors and hung with ornaments each December.

clue.text: A ringer originally -- best ever and least likely

indicators.note: 'originally' points to the origins, the opening letters of the following words

blocks.note: initial letter
initial letter
initial letter
initial letter

explanation.surface: A lookalike that started out superb but ended up the outsider.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell is something that rings, so it is literally a ringer, not a lookalike.

clue.text: Venerable fellow's in bed early

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer is held within the words that follow

blocks.note: running across the two words

explanation.surface: An elderly gentleman who turns in for the night early.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venerable Bede was an eighth-century English monk and historian.
explanation.definitionFit: Bede is always given the title Venerable, so he is the obvious venerable man.

clue.text: Showing no emotion, confront after game

definitions.note: a phrase describing the noun: the expressionless look

indicators.note: 'after' puts the word before it later in the answer than the one following

blocks.note: poker is a card game
to face is to confront

explanation.surface: Keeping a straight face when challenged after a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker face is an expressionless look, the kind card players adopt to hide their hand.

clue.text: Lily, the leading light

blocks.note: first meaning: a white-flowered bulb plant of the lily family
second meaning: the star that guided the Magi to the nativity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading light' usually means a prominent person, but here the light literally led the wise men.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant Ornithogalum bears this name, and so does the star the wise men followed to Christ's birthplace.
